name: Alisos Canyon

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah, Sémillon, Cabernet Franc and Tempranillo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Syrah and Sauvignon Blanc sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
